entries.text: Trespasses are to be first taken to the transgressor for him to remedy his fault.
If your brother trespass against you, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.
We should reprove and admonish one another to prevent sin.
We should receive reproof kindly.
Have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them.
Do not judge others lest you be judged yourselves, for in the way you judge, you will be judged.
Hatred and rejection of reproof of one's faults leads to error, ignorance, remorse and destruction.
Reprove one another that there be no strife or contentions.
Do not reprove and correct others of their ignorance and blindness when you suffer from the same affliction.
He who rebukes a man will find more favor afterward than he who flatters with the tongue.
Admonish those who are unruly.
Reproofs of instruction are the way of life.
Reject a heretick and factious man after the first and second admonition, knowing that such a man is perverted and lost in sin, being self-condemned.
If a brethren is in fault then restore him in a spirit of meekness.
Do not reprove a fool or a scoffer, lest he hate you, for reprove is more effective for a wise man, and he also will love you for it.
You should not refuse to be corrected and reproved by the righteous among you.
Confess your faults to one another.
You are to forgive one another if any one have a quarrel against you.
In meekness instruct and correct those who are in opposition, for perhaps God may give them a change of mind towards an acknowledgment of the truth.
We are exhorted to reprove, rebuke and correct with authority, patience and instruction.
He who heeds reproof gets understanding, and will abide among the wise.
